run.title: Run reproducible labs
run.label: Lab
run.body: Use supplied netlab templates for a three-node topology under containerlab. Live netlab routing and traffic validation is still pending. The separate BGP interop harness runs Ze beside FRR, BIRD, and GoBGP and checks routes through each peer's own CLI.

run.title: Run as a daemon
run.label: Daemon
run.body: Install Ze on an existing Linux host with ze install, then connect through authenticated management. Repeat installation preserves configuration and credentials. Ordinary removal keeps that state, while explicit purge removes it. The guide covers the source build and systemd service. The host keeps its existing interface configuration.

run.title: Run in Docker
run.label: Container
run.body: Build the deployment image, initialize its persistent volume, and run Ze with Compose. Authenticate over SSH and commit configuration changes that survive container recreation on the same volume. The guide covers networking, capabilities, updates and removal. Lab tools use a separate image with a shell.

run.title: Run a VM or appliance
run.label: Appliance
run.body: Build an immutable gokrazy system for QEMU, Proxmox or dedicated hardware. It has a read-only root, persistent configuration and process supervision. The guide covers ISO installation, authenticated SSH, image updates and previous-slot recovery. Source builds produce disk images and installer ISOs. No public image release is available yet.

who.title: Lab router
who.label: Lab
who.body: Network builders can bring up two BGP peers, inspect routes, and check whether Ze's operator tools fit their workflow.

who.title: ExaBGP replacement
who.label: Migration
who.body: ExaBGP users can try the migrator against an existing config and see which process scripts still translate cleanly.

who.title: White-box appliance
who.label: Appliance
who.body: People with spare x86 hardware can boot the appliance image and test the same configuration model without a general-purpose shell.

who.title: Looking glass
who.label: Operate
who.body: Operators who need read-only BGP visibility can publish a looking glass and inspect routes without giving shell access.

who.title: Protocol testbed
who.label: Interop
who.body: Protocol implementers can run Docker interop scenarios against FRR, BIRD, and GoBGP, then turn a failure into a test case.

who.title: AI-assisted operations
who.label: MCP
who.body: MCP exposes Ze commands and structured output to AI tools without a separate command set.
